# go-envoy-oauth — Integration Guide for Agents

> OAuth 2.0 / OIDC reverse-auth gateway implemented as an Envoy HTTP filter.
> This document describes how to integrate with the gateway as an upstream
> service, as a JS/UI client, or as a programmatic API consumer.
>
> Version: {{VERSION}}
> Source: https://github.com/rashpile/go-envoy-oauth

This file is a static, source-only protocol reference. It describes the
open-source contract of the gateway — never the configuration of any
specific deployment. Configured provider names, deployed cookie names,
cluster routing rules, and header overrides are not exposed here. To learn
what *this specific* gateway deployment is configured to do, ask the
operator.

## 1. Overview

This gateway sits in front of one or more upstream services and answers two
questions before any request reaches them:

- Is the caller authenticated? (Have they completed an OAuth flow, do they
  hold a valid bearer token, or do they have an offline-token API key?)
- Are they authorized for the cluster they are calling? (Cluster-level
  rules.)

If yes, the gateway forwards the request to the upstream and injects
identity headers (section 6). If no, the gateway either redirects the
caller to log in (browser flows) or returns a 401/403 (programmatic flows).

Three integration roles read this document:

- **Upstream service implementer** — section 6.
- **JS / browser client** — section 5.
- **Programmatic / API-key client** — section 7.

All roles benefit from sections 2 (endpoint reference), 8 (workflows), and
9 (error responses).

## 2. Endpoint reference

All endpoints are mounted under `/oauth/`. Paths under this prefix bypass
cluster authentication checks — they are the gateway's own endpoints, not
your upstream's.

### `GET /oauth/login`

Initiates the OAuth authorization-code flow. Redirects the browser to the
configured identity provider's authorization endpoint.

Query parameters:

- `redirect_uri` (string, optional) — relative path to redirect back to
  after successful login. Must be a relative path (`/foo/bar`); absolute
  URLs and protocol-relative URLs are rejected with `400 Bad Request`.
  Defaults to `/`.
- `provider` (string, optional) — provider name to log in against.
  Required when the deployment has multiple providers configured. Ignored
  when only one is configured.

Response: `302 Found` with `Location` set to the provider's authorization
URL and an OAuth state cookie set on the response.

### `GET /oauth/callback`

OAuth provider callback. Receives the authorization code, exchanges it
for tokens, fetches user info, and creates a session. The browser is
redirected to the original `redirect_uri` (encoded into the OAuth state).

This endpoint is not called by clients directly — the provider redirects
to it.

Response on success: `302 Found` to the original redirect URI, with a
session cookie set.
Response on failure: `302 Found` to `/`. The user is not stranded on the
callback URL.

### `GET /oauth/logout`

Clears the session cookie and removes the session from the gateway store.

Query parameters:

- `redirect_uri` (string, optional) — relative path to land on after
  logout. Defaults to `/`.

Response: `302 Found` to the redirect URI, with the session cookie
cleared.

### `GET /oauth/welcome`

Optional landing page after login. Useful when the gateway is configured
to land logged-in users on a brand page before bouncing them into the
app.

Query parameters:

- `home-url` (string, optional) — URL for the "Continue to App" button.

Response: `200 text/html`.

### `GET /oauth/user`

Returns the current authenticated user as JSON. Use this from JS/UI
clients to detect login state before rendering authenticated UI.

Response on authenticated request: `200 application/json` with body
shape:

```
{
  "id":       "<user id>",
  "email":    "<user email>",
  "username": "<preferred username, falls back to email>",
  "name":     "<display name>",
  "provider": "<provider name>",
  "claims":   { ... }
}
```

Response on unauthenticated request: `401 Unauthorized` with a short
text body indicating the reason.

JS clients: see section 5 for the recommended fetch pattern.

### `GET /oauth/consent`

Displays the consent page that begins the offline-token (API-key) flow.
Available only when the operator has set `enable_api_key: true`. When
the flag is false, returns `404`.

### `GET /oauth/offline`

Initiates the OAuth offline-access flow that mints a long-lived refresh
token, which the gateway uses to issue API keys for programmatic
clients. Available only when `enable_api_key: true`.

### `GET /oauth/offline-callback`

Provider callback for the offline flow. Issues an API key and shows it
to the user once. Available only when `enable_api_key: true`.

### `GET /oauth/access-denied`

Terminal error page shown when an authenticated user fails authorization
for a cluster.

### `GET /oauth/assets/sso.js`

Optional drop-in JS helper that browser apps can include via
`<script src>`. Provides session-state detection, automatic re-login on
401, and event hooks. Loaded automatically only on clusters where the
operator has set `sso_injection: true`.

Response: `200 application/javascript`.

### `GET /oauth/llms.txt`

This document. Returned as `text/plain; charset=utf-8` with
`Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`. Methods other than `GET` return
`405 Method Not Allowed` with `Allow: GET`.

May be disabled by the operator (`enable_llms_txt: false`). When
disabled, returns `404 Not Found: Unknown OAuth endpoint` —
indistinguishable from any other unknown OAuth path.

## 3. Auth modes

A request gets authorized in one of three ways. The gateway tries them
in order and accepts the first that succeeds.

### 3.1 Session cookie

The default for browsers. Set by `/oauth/callback` after successful
interactive login. The cookie is `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax` by
default; the gateway reads it from `Cookie:` and looks up the session
in its session store.

When a session is missing or expired and the request is for a path that
requires auth:

- If the request `Accept`s `text/html` (browser navigation):
  `302 Found` to `/oauth/login`.
- Otherwise (XHR / fetch / API call): `401 Unauthorized`. Clients must
  NOT retry on 401; they must trigger a full-page reload or call
  `/oauth/login` directly.

### 3.2 Bearer JWT

For API consumers that already hold a JWT issued by the same identity
provider the gateway is configured for. The token is supplied as
`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`. The gateway verifies the signature
against the provider's JWKS and the standard JWT claims (`iss`, `aud`,
`exp`).

Bearer auth is enabled by the operator config flag
`enable_bearer_token` (defaults to enabled).

### 3.3 Offline-token / API key

For headless clients (CLIs, automation, daemons) that cannot complete
an interactive login per request. The user obtains a long-lived API
key once via `/oauth/consent` → `/oauth/offline` →
`/oauth/offline-callback`, then supplies it on each request as one of:

- HTTP header `api-key: <key>` (preferred), or
- HTTP header `x-api-key: <key>` (common variant), or
- Query parameter `?auth-api-key=<key>` (least preferred — the value
  ends up in proxy logs).

API-key auth is enabled by the operator config flag `enable_api_key`
(defaults to disabled for security).

## 4. Session lifecycle

Interactive flow:

1. User navigates to a protected URL with no session cookie.
2. Gateway detects missing cookie. Returns `302` to `/oauth/login`
   (browser) or `401` (XHR — see section 3.1).
3. Login flow runs (sections 2, 8.1).
4. `/oauth/callback` creates the session, sets the cookie, and
   redirects to the original URL.
5. Subsequent requests carry the cookie.
6. The session has an absolute expiry. When the session is past expiry,
   the gateway returns `401` / `302`-to-login as in step 2.
7. `/oauth/logout` clears the cookie and removes the session from the
   store.

The `401`-vs-`403` contract:

- `401 Unauthorized` — caller is not authenticated. Re-login fixes it.
- `403 Forbidden` — caller is authenticated but not authorized for this
  resource/cluster. Re-login does NOT fix it. Clients should show an
  access-denied state and offer "switch account" or contact-admin.

## 5. JS / browser client integration

### 5.1 Detecting login state

Call `GET /oauth/user`:

```
async function whoAmI() {
  const r = await fetch('/oauth/user', { credentials: 'same-origin' });
  if (r.status === 200) return await r.json();
  if (r.status === 401) return null;       // not logged in
  if (r.status === 403) throw new Error('access denied');
  throw new Error('unexpected status ' + r.status);
}
```

### 5.2 Handling 401 from any endpoint

Do NOT retry. Do NOT silently log the user out. Trigger a full-page
reload — the gateway will redirect the navigation to `/oauth/login`
and bring the user back here after they sign in.

```
async function apiCall(path, opts) {
  const r = await fetch(path, { credentials: 'same-origin', ...opts });
  if (r.status === 401) {
    // Session expired or never existed. Reload to trigger re-login.
    window.location.reload();
    return new Promise(() => {}); // never resolves; reload is in progress
  }
  return r;
}
```

### 5.3 Handling 403

Show a terminal error UI. Do NOT reload the page (it will not help —
the user *is* logged in, just not allowed). Typical UX:

- Display "You don't have access to this resource."
- Offer a "Switch account" button that navigates to
  `/oauth/logout?redirect_uri=/oauth/login`.
- Optionally link to `/oauth/access-denied` for the gateway's standard
  access-denied page.

### 5.4 Optional `sso.js` helper

The gateway can be configured to inject
`<script src="/oauth/assets/sso.js" defer>` into HTML responses on
clusters where `sso_injection: true`. The script provides a default
401-handler matching the pattern in 5.2 and a small `window.__sso`
object exposing the current user. This is a convenience; you can
implement the same yourself.

## 6. Upstream service integration

When a request is authenticated and authorized, the gateway forwards
it to the upstream cluster with identity headers added.

### 6.1 Default header names

| Header | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `X-User-ID` | string | session subject (`sub` claim) |
| `X-User-Email` | string | session email claim |
| `X-User-Username` | string | session preferred-username claim, falls back to email |
| `X-Auth-Provider` | string | the configured provider name that authenticated this session |

Deployments may rename any of these via the corresponding
`*_header_name` config keys (see section 10). Upstreams that want to be
portable across deployments should treat the header names as
configuration of their own, not as fixed constants. New upstreams
should *prefer the defaults* listed above unless the operator has
instructed otherwise.

### 6.2 Trust model

Upstream services MUST treat the identity headers as authoritative ONLY
when received from the gateway. Two rules:

1. The gateway strips client-supplied versions of these headers on every
   request, but defense-in-depth requires upstreams to do the same if
   reachable from any path that bypasses the gateway.
2. Do NOT rely on the absence of these headers to mean "anonymous". A
   misconfigured exclusion path could allow an unauthenticated request
   through. If your upstream needs hard authentication, validate the
   bearer token or cookie yourself, or refuse requests that lack the
   identity headers.

### 6.3 Receiving the headers

```
# Pseudocode — read identity headers, refuse if missing
def handler(request):
    user_id = request.headers.get('X-User-ID')
    if not user_id:
        return 401, "missing identity"
    email     = request.headers.get('X-User-Email')
    username  = request.headers.get('X-User-Username')
    provider  = request.headers.get('X-Auth-Provider')
    # ... your business logic ...
```

## 7. API-key / programmatic-client integration

For non-interactive callers (CLIs, automation, server-to-server).

### 7.1 Obtaining an API key (one-time, interactive)

1. Open `/oauth/consent` in a browser.
2. Confirm the consent screen.
3. The gateway redirects through `/oauth/offline` to the provider's
   offline-access flow.
4. The provider redirects back to `/oauth/offline-callback`.
5. The gateway issues an API key and displays it to the user once.
   Save it immediately; it is not retrievable later.

Available only when the operator has set `enable_api_key: true`.

### 7.2 Using the API key

Send the key on every request. In order of preference:

```
api-key: <api-key>
```

```
x-api-key: <api-key>
```

```
GET /api/whatever?auth-api-key=<api-key>
```

Headers are strongly preferred over the query parameter — query
parameters end up in proxy logs and `Referer` headers. Use the query
form only when the client cannot set custom headers.

The gateway exchanges the API key for a fresh access token internally
on each request (cached for the access token's lifetime). No session
cookie is set.

### 7.3 Revoking an API key

API keys are revoked when the underlying offline OAuth session at the
identity provider is revoked, which clients can do by visiting the
provider's account-management UI.

## 8. Workflows

### 8.1 Interactive login

```
Browser              Gateway                  IdP
  | GET /app          |                        |
  |------------------>|                        |
  | 302 /oauth/login  |                        |
  |<------------------|                        |
  | GET /oauth/login  |                        |
  |------------------>|                        |
  | 302 IdP/auth      |                        |
  |<------------------|                        |
  | GET IdP/auth      |                        |
  |--------------------------------------------|
  | (user signs in)                            |
  | 302 /oauth/callback?code=...               |
  |<-------------------------------------------|
  | GET /oauth/callback?code=...               |
  |------------------>|                        |
  |                   | POST IdP/token         |
  |                   |----------------------->|
  |                   | access+id+refresh      |
  |                   |<-----------------------|
  | 302 /app, Set-Cookie: session=...          |
  |<------------------|                        |
  | GET /app, Cookie: session=...              |
  |------------------>|                        |
  |                   | (forward upstream      |
  |                   |  with X-User-* headers)|
```

### 8.2 Logout

```
Browser              Gateway
  | GET /oauth/logout |
  |------------------>|
  | (delete session)  |
  | 302 /, Set-Cookie: session=; max-age=0
  |<------------------|
```

### 8.3 Expired session recovery (XHR)

```
JS                   Gateway
  | fetch /api/x      |
  |------------------>|
  | 401               |
  |<------------------|
  | window.location.reload()
  |
  | GET /current-page (full nav)
  |------------------>|
  | 302 /oauth/login (sees no session)
  |<------------------|
  | (login flow per 8.1)
```

### 8.4 API-key call

```
Client               Gateway              Upstream
  | GET /api/x        |                    |
  | api-key: K        |                    |
  |------------------>|                    |
  |                   | (exchange K for    |
  |                   |  access token,     |
  |                   |  cached)           |
  |                   | (forward with      |
  |                   |  X-User-* headers) |
  |                   |------------------->|
  |                   | 200                |
  |                   |<-------------------|
  | 200               |
  |<------------------|
```

### 8.5 Token refresh (transparent)

The gateway transparently refreshes upstream access tokens using the
stored refresh token. Clients see no extra round trips.

## 9. Error responses

The gateway emits these status codes itself (separate from
upstream-emitted codes):

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `302` | Redirect — to login, callback, welcome, etc. |
| `400` | Bad Request — malformed `redirect_uri` or query parameter. |
| `401` | Unauthorized — no/invalid/expired session, no/invalid bearer, no/invalid API key. |
| `403` | Forbidden — authenticated but not authorized for this cluster. |
| `404` | Not Found — unknown `/oauth/*` endpoint or feature disabled. |
| `405` | Method Not Allowed — wrong HTTP method on a gateway endpoint. |
| `503` | Service Unavailable — identity provider unreachable, JWKS fetch failed. |

Any status code returned from your upstream passes through unchanged.

## 10. Configuration reference (schema)

This section describes the public schema of the gateway's
configuration. It does NOT describe what *this* deployment is
configured with — only the keys, types, and defaults that are valid to
set.

### 10.1 `OAuthConfig` (top-level)

| Key | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer_url` | string | (required, legacy single-provider) | OIDC issuer URL |
| `client_id` | string | (required, legacy) | OAuth client ID |
| `client_secret` | string | (required, legacy) | OAuth client secret |
| `redirect_url` | string | (required, legacy) | OAuth redirect URL |
| `scopes` | string[] | `["openid","profile","email"]` | OAuth scopes |
| `providers` | map<string,ProviderConfig> | empty | Multi-provider configuration |
| `default_provider` | string | (none) | Provider name used when caller does not specify one |
| `session_cookie_name` | string | `session` | Cookie name carrying the session id |
| `session_max_age` | int (seconds) | `86400` (24h) | Session lifetime |
| `session_path` | string | `/` | Cookie path |
| `session_domain` | string | (host-only) | Cookie domain |
| `session_secure` | bool | `true` | Cookie `Secure` flag |
| `session_http_only` | bool | `true` | Cookie `HttpOnly` flag |
| `session_same_site` | string | `Lax` | Cookie `SameSite` (`Strict` / `Lax` / `None`) |
| `user_id_header_name` | string | `X-User-ID` | Header name for user-id injection |
| `user_email_header_name` | string | `X-User-Email` | Header name for email injection |
| `user_username_header_name` | string | `X-User-Username` | Header name for username injection |
| `auth_provider_header_name` | string | `X-Auth-Provider` | Header name for provider-name injection |
| `enable_api_key` | bool | `false` | Enable the API-key (offline-token) flow |
| `enable_bearer_token` | bool | `true` | Enable bearer-JWT authentication |
| `enable_llms_txt` | bool | `true` | Enable the `/oauth/llms.txt` endpoint (this document) |
| `clusters` | map<string,ClusterConfig> | empty | Per-cluster authorization rules |
| `exclude_paths` | string[] | (empty) | Path prefixes exempt from auth; paths with dot-segments or encoded separators never match |
| `remove_headers` | string[] | identity headers above | Headers stripped from inbound requests (defense-in-depth) |

### 10.2 `ClusterConfig` (per-cluster)

| Key | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `exclude` | bool | `false` | Mark this cluster as fully exempt from auth |
| `sso_injection` | bool | `false` | Inject `<script src="/oauth/assets/sso.js">` into HTML responses |
| `sso_appurl` | string | (empty) | Branding URL used by the welcome page for this cluster |
| `sso_appname` | string | (empty) | Branding name used by the welcome page for this cluster |
| `add_token` | bool | `false` | Forward the access token to the upstream as `X-Auth-Token` |
| `provider` | string | (`default_provider`) | Provider this cluster authenticates against |
| `allowed_users` | string[] | empty | Usernames permitted on this cluster (matched against preferred_username, case-insensitive). Use `["*"]` to allow any authenticated user. If empty, the user must match the resolved provider's `allowed_users`; otherwise access is denied. |

Operators may set `enabled: false` on a client in the gateway YAML; such clients are filtered out at the xDS layer and never appear in the `clusters` map below.

The gateway YAML also accepts a free-form `description` string per client. It is operator-facing metadata only and is not propagated into the filter config.

### 10.3 `ProviderConfig` (per-provider)

| Key | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `issuer_url` | string | (required) | OIDC issuer URL |
| `client_id` | string | (required) | OAuth client ID |
| `client_secret` | string | (required) | OAuth client secret |
| `redirect_url` | string | (required) | OAuth redirect URL |
| `scopes` | string[] | `["openid","profile","email"]` | OAuth scopes |
| `allowed_users` | string[] | empty | Lowercased usernames or emails granted access to all clusters served by this provider (OR-grant). Use `["*"]` to permit any authenticated user from this provider. |
